title: No onboarding tests exist
expected_behavior: Onboarding path (register, capability init, trial setup) has automated test coverage
actual_behavior: Zero test files cover the onboarding registration, capability initialization, or trial setup code paths
evidence: grep -r 'onboarding|register|get-started|initCapabilities' lib/__tests__/ returns zero matches
No test file in __shortest__/ covers the full onboarding wizard
blast_radius: Regressions in onboarding are undetected until a real user signs up
recommended_direction: Add integration tests for POST /api/onboarding/register covering capability persistence and trial initialization

title: trial_ends_at uses inline calculation, not TRIAL_DAYS constant
expected_behavior: trial_ends_at calculation uses the TRIAL_DAYS constant from lib/constants.ts
actual_behavior: register/route.ts:185 uses inline Date.now() + 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 instead of importing TRIAL_DAYS
evidence: register/route.ts:185 inline 30-day calculation
lib/constants.ts:8 TRIAL_DAYS = 30 defined but not imported
blast_radius: If TRIAL_DAYS changes, register route would not update. Low risk since both currently equal 30.

title: No API-level capability enforcement
expected_behavior: API routes that create capability-specific resources (bookings, orders, tickets, etc.) verify the business has that capability enabled
actual_behavior: No shared capability-enforcement mechanism was found. Reviewed representative mutation routes (bookings/create-manual, invoices, surveys, polls, queue/call-next, recurring/setup, events/purchase) do not enforce capability eligibility. The only tier check found is in POST /api/invoices (checkTierLimit). All others check only auth and business ownership.
evidence: grep across app/api/ for hasCapability/checkCapability/getEnabledCapabilities — zero matches for access gating
POST /api/bookings/create-manual — authenticateRequest + owner_id only
POST /api/surveys — owner_id only, no capability check
POST /api/polls — owner_id only, no capability check
POST /api/invoices — owner_id + checkTierLimit (tier check but NOT capability check)
POST /api/queue/call-next — authenticateRequest + requireBusinessOwnership only
POST /api/recurring/setup — authenticateRequest + requireBusinessOwnership only
POST /api/events/purchase — public OTP-verified endpoint, no capability check
blast_radius: Direct API calls or custom integrations could create data for disabled capabilities. Dashboard pages without useRequireCapability could also reach these APIs.
recommended_direction: Add capability middleware or per-route checks for capability-specific API routes

batch_1_coverage.enforcement_contract: create_new requires effective; manage_existing/read_history always allowed

title: Free-text intent does not check capability eligibility
expected_behavior: Intent classification considers which capabilities the business has enabled
actual_behavior: parseSmartIntentHybrid classifies text independently of business capabilities. If a customer at a restaurant says 'book an appointment', the intent returns 'booking' even if the restaurant only has ordering enabled. The routing layer (getFirstStepFromCapabilities) prevents the wrong flow from starting, but the intent metadata is wasted.
evidence: smart-intent.ts:521 parseSmartIntentHybrid has no business context parameter
bot.service.ts:939 routing ignores intent for flow selection
blast_radius: Low — the routing layer correctly prevents wrong-flow dispatch. But entity pre-fill from irrelevant intents could cause confusion.
recommended_direction: Pass enabled capabilities to intent classification so it can filter results. Not urgent — routing layer is the safety net.

title: Disabled capability response is generic, not informative
expected_behavior: When a customer requests a capability the business doesn't offer, the bot says something like 'This business doesn't offer X'
actual_behavior: capability-selection.flow.ts:266 returns 'I didn't understand that. Try typing book, order, tickets, or tap View Options to see the menu.' — identical to any parse failure
evidence: capability-selection.flow.ts:266 generic errorMessage
blast_radius: Customer confusion — they know what they want but are told the bot doesn't understand them
recommended_direction: Distinguish between 'capability not offered by this business' vs 'I didn't understand your input'

title: Tier enforcement is client-side only — no server or RLS enforcement
expected_behavior: Server-side or RLS enforcement prevents a business from enabling capabilities above its subscription tier
actual_behavior: Tier check exists only in dashboard UI (canEnableCapability). The RLS policy business_capabilities_owner_update checks only owner_id = auth.uid(). A browser client could directly enable growth/business capabilities on a free plan. During trial all caps are unlocked by design.
evidence: capabilities/page.tsx:148 client-side canToggle()
RLS policy checks owner_id only (migration 182 replaced over-permissive INSERT but didn't add tier check)
No API route exists for capability toggling — direct browser Supabase writes
blast_radius: Business could bypass UI to enable paid capabilities without paying. After trial ends, no downgrade occurs.
recommended_direction: Add RLS check or API route with server-side tier validation for capability writes
product_question: Is the current client-only tier enforcement acceptable during trial? What should happen to growth/business capabilities when a trial ends without upgrade?

title: No automatic capability downgrade when trial expires
expected_behavior: When a 30-day trial ends without the business upgrading, capabilities above the free tier are disabled or restricted
actual_behavior: No cron job, trigger, or webhook handler downgrades capabilities when trial_ends_at passes. Capabilities enabled during trial remain enabled in business_capabilities indefinitely.
evidence: No cron route or Edge Function references trial_ends_at for capability downgrade
app/api/cron/ has trial-check/route.ts but it only sends reminder emails, does not modify capabilities
business_capabilities rows persist with is_enabled=true regardless of trial status
blast_radius: Businesses that never upgrade retain growth/business capabilities permanently after trial
recommended_direction: Either: (a) downgrade capabilities when trial expires, or (b) check trial+tier at runtime (bot/dashboard query time) and filter out ineligible caps
product_question: Should post-trial businesses with free tier lose access to growth/business capabilities? Should this be immediate or grace-period?

title: Human handoff silently fails when chat capability not enabled
expected_behavior: When a customer says 'talk to someone' and the business doesn't have chat enabled, the bot explains that live chat isn't available
actual_behavior: executor.ts:296-330 checks caps.includes('chat'). If chat is not enabled, the escalation block does nothing — the input falls through to the regular flow validator, which treats it as invalid input.
evidence: executor.ts:296-330 escalation regex check
No else branch or customer-facing message when chat is not enabled
blast_radius: Customer asks for human help and gets no acknowledgment — appears as if the bot ignored them
recommended_direction: Add an else branch that tells the customer live chat is not available and offers alternatives

title: Capability initialization failure is silently ignored during onboarding
expected_behavior: initCapabilities() checks the Supabase insert result and propagates errors so onboarding fails atomically or retries
actual_behavior: initCapabilities() (lib/capabilities/service.ts:145-147) awaits the insert but discards the {data, error} return. Supabase insert errors are returned, not thrown — the caller's try/catch (register/route.ts:236-245) cannot catch them. Registration succeeds with zero capability rows. Dashboard and bot enter fallback behavior, potentially replacing user-selected capabilities with category defaults.
evidence: lib/capabilities/service.ts:145-147 — insert result not destructured
app/api/onboarding/register/route.ts:236-245 — try/catch cannot catch non-thrown Supabase errors
app/dashboard/layout.tsx:176-184 — falls back to CATEGORY_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES when no rows
lib/capabilities/service.ts:45-51 — getEnabledCapabilities falls back to getCategoryDefaultCapabilities then CATEGORY_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES
blast_radius: User-selected optional capabilities lost. Business operates on hardcoded category defaults without knowing. Dashboard and bot may show different fallback sets (see CAS-010).
recommended_direction: Destructure insert result, check error, fail onboarding registration or retry. Add integration test for this path.

title: Dashboard and WhatsApp bot use divergent capability-resolution rules
expected_behavior: Dashboard and bot use the same resolver to determine a business's effective capabilities
actual_behavior: Dashboard (layout.tsx:168-184) queries only is_enabled=true rows and falls back to hardcoded CATEGORY_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES. Bot (getEnabledCapabilities in service.ts:13-51) queries ALL rows (enabled and disabled), merges newly-added category defaults not in known set, and falls back to DB-backed getCategoryDefaultCapabilities() first. Concrete divergence: when a new capability default is added to a category after onboarding, the bot auto-enables it but the dashboard does not show it.
evidence: app/dashboard/layout.tsx:168-174 — queries is_enabled=true only, no merge logic
lib/capabilities/service.ts:13-51 — queries all rows, merges new defaults
app/dashboard/layout.tsx:176-184 — hardcoded CATEGORY_DEFAULT_CAPABILITIES fallback
lib/capabilities/service.ts:45-51 — getCategoryDefaultCapabilities (DB-backed) then hardcoded fallback
blast_radius: Bot can expose capabilities the dashboard doesn't show (or vice versa). Fallback paths produce different capability sets when rows are missing. Business cannot see or manage a capability the bot is offering to customers.
recommended_direction: Unify to a single getEffectiveCapabilities() resolver used by both dashboard layout and bot service. The resolver should apply: enabled rows → tier filter → trial override → admin overrides, consistently.
product_question: Should newly-added category defaults auto-enable for existing businesses (bot behavior) or require explicit opt-in (dashboard behavior)?
